questions.question: Which is the formal, preposition-fronted version of "the man who I spoke to"?
questions.explanation: See the Relative clauses lesson for the underlying rule.
answers: The man to whom I spoke.
The man who spoke to me.
The man I spoke to whom.

questions.question: "This is the reason for which the project was delayed" is an example of:
questions.explanation: See the Relative clauses lesson for the underlying rule.
answers: A defining relative clause with a stranded preposition

questions.question: "The committee, to whom the report was submitted, raised no objections" — this register is:
questions.explanation: See the Relative clauses lesson for the underlying rule.

questions.question: Which pair contrasts formal vs. neutral register correctly?
questions.explanation: See the Relative clauses lesson for the underlying rule.
answers: "the man to whom I spoke" (formal) vs. "the man who I spoke to" (neutral)
"the man who I spoke to" (formal) vs. "the man to whom I spoke" (neutral)
Neither is used in modern English
